away.name: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen
away.news: Luukkonen had a dreadful start to the season, allowing 12 goals on 53 shots (.782 SV%) in his first three games (1-2-0), but has been encouraging in his last two outings (2-0-0), saving 48 of 52 shots (.923 SV%). With Alex Lyon (upper body) still sidelined, the Sabres will continue to rely on Luukkonen and hope he can build some momentum from his previous games. The Sabres enter Thursday's contest as -157 home favourites against the 3-3-0 New York Islanders.

home.name: Sergei Bobrovsky
home.news: Anthony Stolarz had a poor showing in Toronto's previous game, a 5-4 loss to the Utah Mammoth, failing to build on momentum from an encouraging opening couple of performances. As a result, the Maple Leafs will turn to Bobrovsky on Thursday. The 38-year-old Bobrovsky was serviceable in his last outing, stopping 30 of 33 shots (.909 SV%) in his first win of the season, a 6-3 win over the Colorado Avalanche. Bobrovsky has a 2.97 GAA and .907 SV% in four games (1-2-1). The Maple Leafs enter Thursday's contest as slight -113 home favourites against a Buffalo Sabres team that has been outscored 26-19 in seven games this season (3-3-1).

away.name: Semyon Varlamov
away.news: Varlamov made his season debut last week, returning to the crease for the first time in nearly two years, and will face the Ottawa Senators on Thursday. The veteran 38-year-old goalie shook off some rust, allowing three goals on 22 shots (.864 SV%) in a 5-2 loss to the New York Rangers, and hopes to return to form with one game under his belt. The Islanders enter action on Thursday as +144 road underdogs against a Senators team off to an impressive 5-2-0 start.

home.name: Linus Ullmark
home.news: Samuel Ersson had a poor showing in Ottawa's previous game, his second start of the season, and will return to his familiar role as understudy to Linus Ullmark, who has started the 2026-27 season tremendously. Ullmark is coming off a poor 2025-26 season, posting a 2.73 GAA and a career-worst .891 SV% in 49 games (28-12-8). That said, the 33-year-old Swedish goalie has been near-perfect this season, posting an absurd 1.27 GAA and a .948 SV% in five games (5-0-0). The Senators enter Thursday's contest as -157 home favourites against a 3-3-0 New York Islanders team.

away.name: Joseph Woll
away.news: Philadelphia will keep its goalie rotation going on Thursday, turning to Joseph Woll in Detroit as they search for their first win of the 2026-27 season in game 9. Despite being winless in four starts to begin his career in Philadelphia, Woll has looked very solid, as proven by his .914 SV% and 2.95 GAA. He heads to Hockeytown to take on the struggling Red Wings, who have won one of their first six games played to start the season.

home.name: Daniil Tarasov
home.news: The struggling 1-3-2 Red Wings will turn to Tarasov to tend the twine for just the second time this season on Thursday against the Philadelphia Flyers. The 27-year-old Tarasov hasn't been called upon much this season, but he was excellent in his only outing, stopping all 30 shots he faced and recording a shutout in a 1-0 shootout loss to the Montreal Canadiens. Tarasov has a favourable matchup on Thursday against the Flyers, one of the few teams that have been more offensively challenged than the Red Wings, scoring just 10 goals in eight games (0-5-3).

away.name: Philipp Grubauer
away.news: Grubauer will start Thursday in Tampa.

home.name: Andrei Vasilevskiy
home.news: Tampa Bay has scored fewer than two goals in three of six games this season (4-2-0), leaving little margin for error for the goaltending. That said, Vasilevskiy, the reigning 2025-26 Vezina Trophy winner, has performed below expectations so far, posting a 2.45 GAA and a lowly .886 SV% in five outings (3-2-0). Tampa Bay enters Thursday's contest as a significant -257 home favourite against the surprisingly potent early-season offence of the Seattle Kraken, who average 4.14 goals per game through seven games (5-2-0).

away.name: Leevi Merilainen
away.news: Kevin Lankinen has started the 2025-26 season abysmal, posting a dreadful 6.88 GAA and .786 SV% in six outings (1-5-0). As a result, the Canucks will roll with Merilainen, who has been their more reliable goalie. Merilainen was solid in his most recent outing, saving 35 of 38 shots (.921 SV%), but he didn't get enough goal support and lost 3-2 to the New York Islanders. The 24-year-old Finnish goalie has a 2.40 GAA and .926 SV% in five appearances (1-1-0). Still, the Canucks enter Thursday's contest as sizeable +252 road underdogs against a Florida Panthers team coming off an impressive 7-3 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets.

home.name: Akira Schmid
home.news: With Jacob Markstrom battling an undisclosed injury, Schmid will tend the twine Thursday against the Vancouver Canucks. Schmid is coming off his first win of the season, saving 24 of 27 shots (.889 SV%) in a 7-3 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets. The 26-year-old Swiss goalie has a 3.72 GAA and .875 SV% in three games this season (1-1-1). The Panthers enter Thursday's contest as significant -296 home favourites against a Vancouver Canucks team that has allowed a league-worst 38 goals through eight games (2-6-0).

away.name: Dylan Garand
away.news: The season-ending injury to Igor Shesterkin sparked panic among the Rangers faithful, but rookie Dylan Garand has been an impressive replacement so far. The 24-year-old Garand was excellent in his most recent outing, saving 25 of 26 shots (.962 SV%) in a 4-1 win over the Tampa Bay Lightning. He has a stellar 1.15 GAA and .951 SV% in four games (3-1-0). The Rangers enter Thursday's contest as +117 road underdogs against a New Jersey Devils team that has scored fewer than two goals in three of their last five games (2-3-0).

home.name: Nico Daws
home.news: Entering the 2026-27 season, the Devils' goaltending tandem of Jake Allen and Nico Daws faced scrutiny after failing to acquire a replacement number-one goalie following Jacob Markstrom's off-season departure. Six games into the season, the Devils have allowed an average of 3.67 goals per game, and the scrutiny has been justified, driven by poor showings from Nico Daws. The 25-year-old Daws has allowed nine goals on 51 shots (.824 SV%) in two games. He hopes to solidify his presence in the crease on Thursday, as the Devils enter action as -134 home favourites against a red-hot 6-2-0 New York Rangers team.

away.name: Stuart Skinner
away.news: Skinner has been stellar early in his tenure with the Jets and will return to the crease on Thursday. The 27-year-old Canadian goalie stopped 19 of 21 shots (.905 SV%) in his most recent outing, a 5-2 win over the Minnesota Wild. He has a 2.47 GAA and .917 SV% in four games this season (3-1-0). The Jets enter action on Thursday as -126 road favourites against a Chicago Blackhawks team coming off a season-high five-goal output in a 5-3 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins.

home.name: Spencer Knight
home.news: The Blackhawks welcomed Connor Bedard (shoulder) back into the lineup for his season debut in a 5-3 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins, a bright note in an otherwise disappointing 2-5-0 start to the season. The team hopes to build on the momentum of their superstar captain's return, turning to Knight to tend the twine on Thursday. The 25-year-old Knight had a solid first full season in Chicago, but has a subpar 3.64 GAA and .885 SV% through five games this season (2-3-0). Chicago enters Thursday's contest as +114 home underdogs against a surprising 4-1-1 Winnipeg Jets team.

away.name: Alex Nedeljkovic
away.news: Yaroslav Askarov's start to the season has been underwhelming, posting an ugly 3.99 GAA and .848 SV% in five games (2-3-0), which makes Nedeljkovic's lack of action this season somewhat surprising. The 30-year-old Nedeljkovic was excellent in his only outing this season, saving 24 of 26 shots (.923 SV%) in a 3-2 overtime win over the St. Louis Blues. The Sharks enter Thursday as +121 road underdogs against a Nashville Predators team that has lost three of its last four (1-3-0).

home.name: Juuse Saros
home.news: With Justus Annunen still navigating an undisclosed injury, the Predators will continue to rely on Saros. Saros is coming off his worst performance in the young 2026-27 season, allowing five goals on 25 shots (.800 SV%) in a 5-2 loss to the Vegas Golden Knights. The 31-year-old Finnish goalie has a 3.17 GAA and .897 SV% in five games (2-2-1). The Predators enter Thursday as -135 home favourites against a San Jose Sharks team that has scored just seven goals in its last four games (1-3-0).

away.name: Joel Hofer
away.news: Hofer led the Blues onto the ice for warmups.

home.name: Jesper Wallstedt
home.news: Wallstedt has been busy with Filip Gustavsson (hip) sidelined, and he got his first night off in Minnesota's previous game, but the team fared poorly without him, losing 5-2 to the Winnipeg Jets. Wallstedt emerged as Minnesota's starting goalie in the playoffs and has carried that momentum into the 2026-27 season. The 23-year-old Swedish goalie has an outstanding 1.82 GAA and .933 SV% in six games (4-1-1). Minnesota enters Thursday's contest as -140 home favourites against a St. Louis Blues team on a two-game winning streak.

away.name: Karel Vejmelka
away.news: Vejmelka hasn't been outstanding this season, but his 4-1-0 record has helped Utah get off to a strong start. The 30-year-old Czech goalie allowed four goals on 26 shots (.846 SV%) in his most recent game, but received enough goal support to salvage a 5-4 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs. He has a 2.46 GAA and .895 SV% this season. The Mammoth enter Thursday's contest as slight -112 road favourites against the high-flying Edmonton Oilers, who average 4.8 goals per game through six games this season (5-0-1).

home.name: Devon Levi
home.news: The Oilers have struggled between the pipes in recent seasons, but they hope Levi can provide long-overdue stability after a promising start to the 2026-27 season. The 24-year-old Levi has yet to lose in four games this season (4-0-0), posting a 2.76 GAA and .903 SV%, and is coming off an outstanding performance, saving 39 of 40 shots (.975 SV%) in a 4-1 win over the Los Angeles Kings. The Oilers enter Thursday's contest as slight -110 home favourites against a Central Division-leading Utah Mammoth team that has scored 27 goals (3.9 GF/GP) in seven games (5-2-0).

away.name: Dustin Wolf
away.news: After a 0-5-0 start, the Flames hope to build momentum off their first win of the season, improving to 1-5-0. Wolf was instrumental in the win, saving 23 of 25 shots (.920 SV%) to defeat the Anaheim Ducks 4-2. The 25-year-old American goalie has a 4.56 GAA and .839 SV% in four games (1-3-0). The Flames enter Thursday’s contest as significant +266 road underdogs against a 6-2-0 Vegas Golden Knights team.

home.name: Carter Hart
home.news: After leading Vegas to the Stanley Cup Finals last season, Hart has been favoured between the pipes early in the 2026-27 season and will return to the crease on Thursday. The 28-year-old goalie allowed three goals on 27 shots (.889 SV%) in his most recent game, a 4-2 loss to the Minnesota Wild. He has a 2.41 GAA and .906 SV% in five games (3-2-0). The Golden Knights enter Thursday's contest as significant -308 home favourites against a Calgary Flames team that has only scored 12 goals this season (1-5-0).
